hints: Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium: $T_A\cos 50^\circ = T_B\cos 10^\circ$.
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium: $T_A\sin 50^\circ - T_B\sin 10^\circ = mg = 20(10) = 200\text{ N}$.
Solve the simultaneous equations by expressing $T_B$ in terms of $T_A$ and substituting into the vertical equation.
walkthrough: The small object $P$ of mass $20\text{ kg}$ is in equilibrium under three forces: the tension $T_A$ in string $A$, the tension $T_B$ in string $B$, and the downward weight $W = mg = 20 \times 10 = 200\text{ N}$.

Set up the horizontal equilibrium equation (taking right as positive):
$$T_A\cos 50^\circ - T_B\cos 10^\circ = 0$$
$$T_B = T_A\frac{\cos 50^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the vertical equilibrium equation (taking up as positive):
$$T_A\sin 50^\circ - T_B\sin 10^\circ - 200 = 0$$
$$T_A\sin 50^\circ - T_B\sin 10^\circ = 200 \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$

Put over a common denominator of $\cos 10^\circ$:
$$T_A\left(\frac{\sin 50^\circ\cos 10^\circ - \cos 50^\circ\sin 10^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ}\right) = 200$$

Use the sine addition formula $\sin(A - B) = \sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B$ where $A = 50^\circ$ and $B = 10^\circ$:
$$\sin 50^\circ\cos 10^\circ - \cos 50^\circ\sin 10^\circ = \sin(50^\circ - 10^\circ) = \sin 40^\circ$$
$$T_A\frac{\sin 40^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} = 200$$

Multiply by $\cos 10^\circ$ and divide by $\sin 40^\circ$:
$$T_A = \frac{200\cos 10^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ} = \frac{200(0.984808)}{0.642788} = \frac{196.9615}{0.642788} \approx 306.42\text{ N} \approx 306\text{ N}$$

Now find $T_B$ using Equation 1. Because $\cos 50^\circ = \sin(90^\circ - 50^\circ) = \sin 40^\circ$:
$$T_B = \left(\frac{200\cos 10^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ}\right) \times \frac{\cos 50^\circ}{\cos 10^\circ} = 200 \times \frac{\cos 50^\circ}{\sin 40^\circ} = 200 \times 1 = 200\text{ N}$$
